# sonarqube_new_code_periods (Resource)

The new code definition, globally, for a project or for a branch. Destroying it reverts to the inherited definition (the global one reverts to PREVIOUS_VERSION). Import ID: `global`, `project` or `project/branch`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Instance-wide default.
resource "sonarqube_new_code_periods" "global" {
  type  = "NUMBER_OF_DAYS"
  value = "30"
}

# A project that compares against its main branch.
resource "sonarqube_new_code_periods" "api" {
  project = "example-api"
  type    = "REFERENCE_BRANCH"
  value   = "main"
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `type` (String) `PREVIOUS_VERSION`, `NUMBER_OF_DAYS`, `REFERENCE_BRANCH` or `SPECIFIC_ANALYSIS`.

### Optional

- `branch` (String) Branch name. Requires project.
- `project` (String) Project key. Omit for the global definition.
- `value` (String) Days for NUMBER_OF_DAYS, branch for REFERENCE_BRANCH, analysis key for SPECIFIC_ANALYSIS.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Identifier of this resource in Terraform state.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import sonarqube_new_code_periods.example 'example-api'
```
